theme.title: Courtside Curiosities
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: The chart shows three other champions' regular seasons. How many games did Kawhi Leonard's 2018–19 Raptors win?
questions.context: Toronto · Kawhi Leonard's lone Raptors season
questions.note: 58–24, second in the East behind Milwaukee, the team Toronto beat in six in the East finals.

funFacts.text: Toronto exchanged DeMar DeRozan, Jakob Poeltl and a protected pick for Kawhi Leonard and Danny Green.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: DeMar DeRozan (who spent his first nine seasons in the NBA with the Raptors)

funFacts.text: The Raptors added Marc Gasol from Memphis at the trade deadline for a package led by Jonas Valančiūnas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Memphis Grizzlies traded Marc Gasol to the Raptors

funFacts.text: Nick Nurse was promoted from assistant coach after Toronto dismissed Dwane Casey.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Raptors promoted assistant coach Nick Nurse as their head coach

questions.prompt: Memphis beat Oklahoma City by a record 73 points in December 2021. How many points did the Grizzlies' bench score?
questions.note: 93, more than the 79 the entire Thunder team scored in the 152–79 rout.

funFacts.text: Before this game, the record margin belonged to Cleveland, which beat Miami by 68 points.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The previous record was a Cleveland Cavaliers 68–point blowout win over the Miami Heat

funFacts.text: The final score was 152–79, and the game was played on December 2, 2021.
That season Memphis won the Southwest Division for the first time in franchise history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They also won the Southwest division title for the first time in Grizzlies' franchise history

questions.prompt: Over 19 seasons, how many games did John Stockton miss?
questions.note: 22 in 19 seasons; he retired as the NBA's career leader in both assists and steals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: missing only 22 games in his 19-season career and playing every game of 17 seasons

funFacts.text: Stockton had completed 17 full seasons without missing a single game.
His most significant injury was a left-knee MCL problem that kept him out at the start of 1997–98.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: due to an injured MCL in his left knee sustained in the preseason

funFacts.text: He was still Utah's starting point guard when he retired at age 41.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He remained a starting NBA player until his retirement at age 41

questions.prompt: Wilt Chamberlain averaged 50.4 points in 1961–62. What did Elgin Baylor average that season while on Army weekend passes?
questions.note: 38.3, the highest average ever by anyone other than Chamberlain, with 18.6 rebounds.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: averaging 38.3 points (the highest average in NBA history by any player other than Chamberlain)

funFacts.text: Called to active duty as an Army reservist, he could join the Lakers only on weekend passes.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: he could play for the Lakers only when on a weekend pass.

funFacts.text: He also averaged 18.6 rebounds that season.
That spring he scored 61 points in a Finals game against Boston, a Finals record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor set the still-standing NBA record for points in an NBA Finals game with 61.

questions.prompt: The chart shows other famous comebacks. How far behind did Anthony Edwards's Timberwolves fall before their 2024 Game 7 win at Denver?
questions.note: 20 points, the largest Game 7 comeback in playoff history, against the defending champions.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Timberwolves overcame a 20–point deficit to win game 7 against the Nuggets, the largest game 7 comeback in NBA playoffs history.

funFacts.text: Minnesota returned to the West finals after a long wait.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Minnesota also reached the Western Conference finals for the second time in franchise history, after 2004.

funFacts.text: Jamal Murray carried Denver early in the contest.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jamal Murray's 24 first-half points gave the Nuggets a 15-point halftime lead

funFacts.text: The Wolves swung momentum with a dominant third-quarter run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they closed the third quarter with a 28–9 run and took the lead in the fourth
